extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, third-party requesters, patent owners, and USPTO reexamination staff (CRU/examiners)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and filing standards governing inter partes reexamination requests and subsequent prosecution at the USPTO Central Reexamination Unit (CRU), including filing content, addressing, processing, assignment, access, fees, and workflow/timing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mail stop and addressing for reexamination correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: All requests for inter partes reexamination (original request papers) and all subsequent inter partes reexamination correspondence mailed via U.S. Postal Service should be addressed to: Mail Stop 'Inter Partes Reexam', Attn: Central Reexamination Unit, Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450. Hand-carried or delivery-service correspondence should be carried to the Customer Service Window, Randolph Building, 401 Dulany Street, Alexandria, VA 22314 and marked 'Mail Stop Inter Partes Reexam.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is strongly recommended that the Mail Stop information be placed in a prominent position on the first page of each paper being filed utilizing a sufficiently large font size that will direct attention to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: No FAX for initial request (filing) and corrected/complete requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for inter partes reexamination may not be sent by facsimile transmission (FAX). This prohibition also applies to a corrected/completed request sent in response to a notice that the original request was not filing-date-compliant, since the corrected/completed request stands in place of, or is a completion of, the original request papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All subsequent inter partes reexamination correspondence, however, may be FAXed to the Central Reexamination Unit at (571) 273-9900.

rubrics_metrics.name: EFS‑Web acceptance of reexamination requests and follow‑on papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective July 9, 2007, the USPTO accepts requests for reexamination and 'follow-on' papers (subsequent correspondence in reexamination proceedings) submitted via the Office's Web-based electronic filing system (EFS-Web).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Legal Framework for EFS-Web for current details and requirements (link provided in MPEP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of proceeding in correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing the request for inter partes reexamination, any letters sent to the Office relating to the reexamination proceeding should identify the proceeding by the number of the patent undergoing reexamination, the reexamination request control number assigned, the name of the examiner, and the examiner's Art Unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of certificate of mailing/transmission and Express Mail procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The certificate of mailing and transmission procedures (37 CFR 1.8) may be used to file any paper in an inter partes reexamination proceeding, except for a request for reexamination and a corrected/replacement request for reexamination. The 'Express Mail' mailing procedure (37 CFR 1.10) may be used to file any paper in an inter partes reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 512 for certificate of mailing/transmission use and MPEP § 513 for Express Mail procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for amendments and other papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and other papers filed on behalf of patent owners must be signed by the patent owners, or the registered attorney or agent of record in the patent file, or any registered attorney or agent acting in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double correspondence with the patent owners and the attorney or agent normally will not be undertaken by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address default and communications to patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications from the Office to the patent owner will be directed to the correspondence address for the patent being reexamined (see 37 CFR 1.33(c)). Where no correspondence address is specified, correspondence will be with the most recent attorney or agent made of record by the patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized/untimely papers prior to initial Office action (37 CFR 1.939)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an unauthorized paper is filed by any party at any time during the inter partes reexamination proceeding it will not be considered and may be returned. Unless otherwise authorized, no paper shall be filed prior to the initial Office action on the merits of the inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers directed to the merits of the reexamination other than permitted categories (e.g., citations under 37 CFR 1.501 and 1.933, another complete request under 1.510 or 1.915, or notifications under MPEP § 2686) filed before the first Office action will be returned or expunged; copies of returned/expunged papers are not retained but a record of the return/expungement is made in the patent file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and entry of prior art citations (37 CFR 1.902/1.933/1.915/1.948)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations by the patent owner in accordance with § 1.933 and by an inter partes reexamination third party requester under § 1.915 or § 1.948 will be entered in the inter partes reexamination file. The entry in the patent file of other citations submitted after the date of an order for reexamination by persons other than the patent owner or the third party requester will be delayed until the inter partes reexamination proceeding has been concluded by issuance and publication of a reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.502 for processing of prior art citations in patent and reexamination files during an ex parte reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date for a request (37 CFR 1.919 / content under 1.915)
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a request for inter partes reexamination is the date on which the request satisfies all the requirements for the request set forth in § 1.915. Request papers that fail to satisfy all the requirements of 37 CFR 1.915 are incomplete and will not be granted a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request does not include required fees or meet paragraph (b) requirements, the requester will be notified and generally given an opportunity to complete the request within a specified time; failure to comply will result in no filing date and placement of the request in the patent file as a citation if it complies with § 1.501.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Failure to Comply and one‑opportunity-to‑cure principle
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Central Reexamination Unit determines the request fails to meet one or more filing date requirements, the person identified as requesting reexamination will be notified (Form PTOL-2076) and generally given an opportunity (generally 30 days) to complete the requirements of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent extraordinary circumstances, requester will be given only one opportunity to correct non-compliance. A single failure to comply with the notice will ordinarily result in the request not being granted a filing date. If defects are not remedied, a 'Notice of Disposition of Inter Partes Reexamination Request' (PTOL-2078) will be prepared identifying uncorrected defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision vacating filing date discovered after initial assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after a filing date and control number are assigned, the examiner notes a non-compliance item not earlier recognized, a memo is forwarded and OPLA may issue a decision vacating the assigned reexamination filing date. The requester will be notified of the non-compliant items and given time to correct them; absent extraordinary circumstances, only one opportunity to correct is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes discovery of returned checks or stopped payments after a filing date but before a decision on the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication/Notice of filing in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of filing of all complete requests for inter partes reexamination will be published in the Official Gazette approximately 4-5 weeks after filing and will be announced under the heading 'Requests for Inter Partes Reexamination Filed' including the name of any requester and other items set forth in 37 CFR 1.11(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A record of requests filed will also be located in the Patent Search Room and in the reexamination preprocessing area of the CRU, and PALM can be used to determine if a request has been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive notice to patent owner via Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is not possible to deliver mail to the patent owner because no current address is available and all efforts to correspond fail, the reexamination proceeding will proceed without the patent owner; publication in the Official Gazette of the notice of filing of the inter partes reexamination request will serve as constructive notice to the patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of corrections to incomplete requests in CRU preprocessing
rubrics_metrics.description: All processing of submissions to cure an incomplete request for inter partes reexamination is carried out in the preprocessing area of the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU). Such submissions should be marked 'Mail Stop Inter Partes Reexam' so they are promptly forwarded to reexamination preprocessing staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2627 for details on incomplete requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to reexamination files via Public PAIR
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination files are open to inspection by the general public via Public PAIR on the USPTO Internet site; members of the public can view the entire content of the reexamination file with the exception of non-patent literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To access, follow specific steps on the USPTO site (Site Index → Electronic Business Center → Status & View Documents → search by Control Number). Copies may be ordered from Document Services Division or obtained from IFW via PAIR; certified copies available on CD-ROM.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM/IFW methods to determine if a reexamination request was filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions are provided to determine on PALM (Internet and Intranet) if a reexamination request has been filed for a given patent number, including steps to search by Patent Number and to view 'Continuity Data' where related reexamination numbers (90/ for ex parte, 95/ for inter partes) are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There may be about a ten (10) day lag between filing and data entry into the PALM database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workflow timing and consultation requirements for assignment and decision preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: After assignment to an examiner, the examiner will, no later than one week after receipt of the inter partes reexamination file, prepare for an initial consultation conference with the Reexamination Legal Advisor (RLA) and notify the CRU SPE of availability. The consultation should be completed within two weeks of forwarding to the examiner. After the consultation, the examiner will prepare a decision on the request and, where applicable, a first Office action no later than two weeks from the date of the consultation conference (unless otherwise authorized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CRU SPE will have one week to review and obtain corrections; at the latest, the decision/action must be forwarded to the RLA within nine weeks of the filing date (unless otherwise authorized). RLA performs final review prior to mailing. In rare cases a first action may not accompany the order granting reexamination (see MPEP § 2660).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of patent owner responses and further prosecution workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a patent owner response (and permitted third party requester comments), the file is messaged to the examiner who reviews responses, decides on a proposed course of action, consults with the RLA (with CRU SPE or Technology Center QAS present), and prepares the appropriate action which is then reviewed and mailed. Further prosecution and examination follow similarly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2671.03 for panel review prior to issuing Office actions, § 2676 for appeal conferences, and § 2677 for Examiner’s Answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee processing, fee types, and small entity reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: All fees in an inter partes reexamination proceeding (including the filing request fee, excess claim fees for claims added by the patent owner, extension of time fees under 37 CFR 1.956, and fees for appeals/briefs/oral hearings under 37 CFR 41.20(b)) are processed by the CRU and posted via the RAM program. Petitions under 37 CFR 1.137/1.182/1.183 require fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee is required for issuance of a reexamination certificate. Small entity reductions under 35 U.S.C. 41(h)(1) are available for certain fees (appeal, brief, oral hearing, excess claims, certain petitions) but are not available for the reexamination filing fee, extension of time fees, nor for certain petition fees. In merged proceedings only a single fee is needed even if multiple copies of submissions are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM record systems, e-file, status codes, and reporting events
rubrics_metrics.description: The PALM system supports reexamination processing: (A) retrieval of reexamination file data, (B) reexamination e-File via IFW, (C) patent file location control for paper-only files, (D) reporting major events to PALM, and (E) status/tickler reports for Technology Centers. Reexamination proceedings have status codes in the '400' or '800' range; patent applications use other ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events to report include determinations mailed (grant/denial), petitions received, decisions on petitions (granted/denied), mailing of examiner actions, patent owner responses, and third party requester comments. All events are permanently recorded and displayed in the 'Contents' portion of PALM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment policy for reexamination examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination requests will normally be assigned to the CRU art unit which examines the technology in which the patent is classified. The CRU SPE assigns the reexamination to a primary examiner other than the examiner that originally examined the patent; normally the new examiner should be most familiar with the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The general policy is to avoid assigning to any examiner who participated in the original examination (including conferees). Exceptions: when the original examiner is the only examiner with adequate knowledge of the technology—such an assignment must be approved by the CRU Director and that approval must be stated in the decision. If an earlier reexamination is still ongoing, the same examiner may be assigned the new reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment handling where reissue and reexamination are copending or merged
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reissue application is pending for a patent and a reexamination request is filed for the same patent, the reexamination request is generally assigned to an examiner who did not examine the original patent application even though the original examiner may be handling the reissue application. If reexamination is granted and the reissue and reexamination proceedings are merged, the merged proceeding will generally be conducted in the TC and handled by a TC examiner other than the examiner who examined the original patent application; the reissue application would be transferred from the originally assigned examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a reexamination is pending and a reissue is filed, related reassignment procedures apply (see MPEP § 2686.03).
